sources.entry: Peer-to-peer file sharing is the distribution and sharing of digital media using peer-to-peer (P2P) networking technology.

summary.name: Peer-to-peer file sharing
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia overview of peer-to-peer (P2P) file sharing, covering how decentralized networks distribute digital media, their history, and the economic, legal and security debates around them.
use_cases: understanding how P2P file sharing networks work
researching the history of Napster, Gnutella and BitTorrent
reading about copyright and legal issues in file sharing
learning about privacy and security risks of P2P software
studying the economics of file sharing
summary.what_it_does: This is an encyclopedia article rather than a software tool. It explains that P2P file sharing lets users find and transfer files such as music, movies, books and games directly between computers on a network. It traces the shift from centralized servers (Napster, eDonkey2000) to decentralized networks (Gnutella, Kazaa, LimeWire) and then to BitTorrent, which has no built-in search and is hard to shut down. The page also covers economic debates over music and film losses, public usage polls, privacy and malware risks, and copyright law.
notable: Traces the evolution from centralized (Napster) to decentralized (Gnutella, BitTorrent) P2P designs
Explains why BitTorrent is hard to shut down: no single owner and no built-in search
Covers economic, legal and privacy debates, including inadvertent exposure of sensitive data
caveats: Describes historical services; several named networks (Kazaa, Morpheus, LimeWire) are stated to have shut down
Economic impact figures are disputed and some are from industry or unofficial studies
